title: A fingerprint for a replacement plan

blocks.text: A water utility replaces old mains. Its plan is a dict from a main's id to the year it is replaced, for example `{"M07": 2028, "M12": 2027}`. The audit team stores one short id per plan, so that two runs can be compared at a glance and an old plan can be found again by its id.

Write `fingerprint(plan)`. It returns 16 lowercase hex characters. Two plans with the same entries get the same id, whatever order their dicts were built in and in whichever Python process the id is computed. Plans whose entries differ in any way get different ids. Python's `hash()` is not an option for this; the page says why.

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json


def fingerprint(plan: dict[str, int]) -> str:
    """16 hex characters naming the plan: the same in every process, different for different plans."""
    text = json.dumps(sorted(plan.items()), separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(fingerprint({"M07": 2028, "M12": 2027}))

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from fingerprint import fingerprint

plan = {"P02": 2031, "P09": 2030, "P14": 2032}

print("id of the plan:", fingerprint(plan))
print("id, same plan built backwards:", fingerprint(dict(reversed(list(plan.items())))))
print("id, P09 moved to 2031:", fingerprint({**plan, "P09": 2031}))

cases.says: the same plan gives the same id, and moving one main to another year gives another id
two dicts with the same entries, built in different orders, are the same plan
two fresh Python processes with different hash seeds give the same id
main M1 in year 12 and main M11 in year 2 are different plans
